title: Thames Insurance outreach scratchpad
content:
Quick personal scratchpad for Thames Insurance play. Not a polished deck — working notes + outbound drafts + rebuttals + next steps. Keep short, iterate after call.

Account snapshot
- Name: Thames Insurance (mid-sized carrier, US regional, heavy on broker integrations)
- HQ: London (US subsidiary in NJ)
- Estimated infra: mix of cloud (GCP, Azure) + private data center for PII workloads
- Primary drivers: claims automation, customer self-service, agent assist, cost containment on inference for high-volume chat/FAQ flows
- Regulatory notes: must support data residency (US-only for PII), SOC2/ISO controls, potential upcoming EU/regional constraints for some lines

Key contacts (to confirm on discovery)
- Head of AI/Automation: likely "Sanjay Patel" (LinkedIn shows automation lead) — target for technical decisioning
- Platform lead / infra: "Marina Lopez" — owns cloud infra and security approvals
- Product (Claims): "Owen Blake" — business owner for claims automation POC
- Procurement: "K. Nguyen" — pricing and contract

Why Redwood might matter to them (value props trimmed to likely pain)
- Predictable latency for policy lookup and agent assist (need sub-200ms 95p for chat flows)
- Dedicated pools to isolate PII models + private deployment option (fits compliance)
- Cost controls: batching suggestions + quantization guidance to lower token unit costs for high-volume claims text gen
- Rollout/observability: per-route cost/latency + eval-driven quality regression alerts — helps safety/regression for actuarial prompts
- Graceful degradation: fallback to smaller quantized model for peak windows (important for SLAs)

Possible POC scope (quick options to propose)
1) Claims triage assistant (30-day POC)
   - Ingest structured claim notes -> triage category + suggested severity + structured output (JSON)
   - Success metric: reduce manual triage time by 30% and precision of suggested category > 85% on sample set
   - Deployment: Dedicated pool (single-tenant) or Private trial in their VPC for PII
2) Broker-facing FAQ/chat (60-day)
   - High-concurrency chat with prefix caching + KV caching for policy context (cost reduction)
   - SLO target: 95p latency < 250ms for short responses

Outbound subject lines to test (A/B)
- "Quick question about claims automation at Thames"
- "30-day pilot to cut claims triage time — Redwood"
- "Low-latency, private LLM inference for regulated insurers"

Cold email draft (first touch)
Hi Sanjay —

I’m Marcus at Redwood Inference. We help regulated carriers run low-latency, cost-predictable LLM inference in ways that meet SOC2 and VPC requirements. I read about Thames’ push to automate claims triage — curious if you’d be open to a 20-minute call to explore a short pilot that demonstrates 30% triage time reduction while keeping data in your VPC.

If helpful, I can share a short case study and an extremely lightweight pilot plan. Are you available next week for a quick chat?

Thanks,
Marcus

Follow-up (if no reply after 3 days)
- Quick note to check if you saw my previous message — we can scope a non-production pilot that uses synthetic data to prove latency and cost without touching live PII.

Call prep checklist (for discovery)
- Confirm latency SLOs for agent assist and chat flows
- Clarify data residency / whether synthetic or anonymized data is acceptable for PoC
- Ask about current model endpoints (vendor stack, self-hosted vs managed) and rough token volume per month
- Identify procurement timeline & security review owners
- Ask for a small sample dataset or anonymized transcripts

Common objections + suggested rebuttals
1) "We can build this ourselves / already have a model infra team"
   - Rebuttal: acknowledge capability; highlight ops lift to keep low-latency production-grade and the hidden costs (kernel selection, batching, KV cache tuning). Offer a 2-week technical spike to show time-to-value difference.
2) "Cost — per token pricing will explode with our volume"
   - Rebuttal: discuss Dedicated pricing + Optimize tools (batching, quantization) that reduce unit costs; propose a cap/burst policy for first 90 days to control spend while measuring ROI.
3) "Security/compliance — can't send PII"
   - Rebuttal: private deploy option (VPC/on-prem), KMS integrations, and audit logs. Suggest initial PoC on synthetic/anonymized data. Reference SOC2 and enterprise support options.
4) "Vendor lock-in / migration risk"
   - Rebuttal: emphasize model/version pinning, standard APIs, exportable KV caches and canary rollouts; we can run a short export proof to show portability.

Competitive notes (intel)
- Vendor X: cheap hosting but poor observability + no private VPC option (risk for Thames)
- Vendor Y: offers on-prem (appliance) but slow rollout and no structured output tooling for claims workflows

Measurement plan for POC
- Latency: p95 / p99 per route measured with Redwood Console traces
- Cost: tokens per inference + unit cost pre/post batching/quantization; reporting weekly
- Quality: labeled prompt set / eval harness — track recall/precision for triage categories

Personal TODOs before outreach
- Ask Solutions Eng for quick benchmark for sample transcripts (request: 100 anonymized claim notes, can we run on Redwood hosted + Dedicated to show delta?) — assigned Aisha
- Draft a one-page pilot plan + pricing tier options (cost estimate for 30-day PoC) — assigned me
- Prep short slide (3 slides) on security + deployment options for Marina

Misc notes / open questions
- Confirm Thames’ monthly token volume (approx) — needed for pricing model
- Check if they currently use any embedding pipelines (we could propose hybrid retrieval + generation to reduce cost)
- Is there a broker partner that will require MFA/SAML integration? Could affect private deployment timelines.

Meeting seed agenda (20 min)
1) Intros + problem framing (3 min)
2) Current infra & pain points (5 min)
3) Overview of Redwood fit + POC options (7 min)
4) Next steps & approvals (5 min)

Bottom line for first outreach: be concise, lead with compliance + latency + cost predictability. Keep ask: 20-min intro + permission to share 1-pager.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate after first response.
